title: Cloudflare Makes Basin Serverless Analytics Generally Available
gist: Cloudflare has made Basin, its serverless analytics platform built on Apache Iceberg and R2 with zero egress fees, generally available; it bundles ingestion, catalog and distributed SQL to target teams too small for a full warehouse, as AWS and Google also push unified analytics.

insights.claim: Cloudflare's Basin, now generally available, is a serverless analytics platform built on Apache Iceberg and R2 Object Storage that integrates with DuckDB, Snowflake and Apache Spark with no data egress fees.
insights.speaker: Renato Losio
insights.so_what: Cloudflare (NET) is expanding from edge networking into data/analytics revenue.
insights.locator: Cloudflare has announced the general availability of Basin

insights.claim: Basin combines three services: Basin Pipelines ingests events from Workers, HTTP and Logpush with SQL transforms; Basin Catalog manages Iceberg metadata and table maintenance; Basin SQL provides a serverless distributed query engine.
insights.speaker: Renato Losio
insights.so_what: A full ingest-to-query stack on Cloudflare's network increases platform lock-in and attach rates for Workers/R2.

insights.claim: Since preview, Cloudflare raised Basin ingestion capacity to 3 GB/s per stream and added Logpush integration and Terraform support; real-time processing, newest Iceberg spec support, adaptive maintenance and data-sovereignty controls are planned with no committed dates.
insights.speaker: Renato Losio
insights.so_what: Roadmap gaps (real-time, sovereignty) limit near-term enterprise displacement of incumbents.
insights.locator: Since its preview, Basin has increased ingestion capacity

insights.claim: Cloudflare argues data portability across Iceberg-compatible engines is only possible with free egress, and cites growth of the open Apache Iceberg ecosystem as a main driver of Basin.
insights.speaker: Renato Losio
insights.so_what: Zero egress plus open table formats erodes hyperscaler data-gravity moats and warehouse lock-in.
insights.quote: That kind of data portability is only possible with free egress
insights.locator: Marc Selwan, senior product manager at Cloudflare

insights.claim: A PashaPay lead data analyst says Basin will not knock Snowflake off its spot soon, but serves a large market layer of teams whose data is too small for dedicated infrastructure and too big for Excel.
insights.speaker: Renato Losio
insights.so_what: Basin is a mid-market/SMB play rather than a direct near-term threat to Snowflake's core warehouse business.
insights.quote: there's a big layer of the market made up of teams whose data is too small to justify dedicated infrastructure and too big to fit in Excel

insights.claim: Unified analytics is a crowded push: AWS acquired DuckLabs and integrated DuckDB into Aurora PostgreSQL, and Google has repositioned BigQuery as a unified AI-ready data platform.
insights.speaker: Renato Losio
insights.so_what: Lakehouse/analytics convergence intensifies competition and pricing pressure on standalone warehouse vendors.
insights.locator: Cloudflare is not the only cloud provider
